ordered_diagnoses: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction

facts.raw_span: dyspnea and syncope during exercise
essential hypertension and Parkinson disease
dyspnea on exertion and exercise intolerance for the past year
difficulty walking more than 100m
elevated blood pressure of 150/78 mm Hg
normal breath and heart sounds without any murmurs
Hemogram, serum electrolytes, and thyroid function test were within normal limits
Normal left ventricular ejection fraction (74%)
Left atrial enlargement (volume index, 34.89 mL/m2)
Pulmonary hypertension (mean pulmonary arterial pressure 32 mm Hg)
sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block (PR interval 360 ms)
third-degree AV block with minimum heart rate of 36 beats/min

concepts.why: The patient has elevated blood pressure and left atrial enlargement, which are indicative of hypertensive heart disease.
The patient has a mean pulmonary arterial pressure of 32 mm Hg, which is diagnostic of pulmonary hypertension.
The patient has first-degree and third-degree atrioventricular block, which is a conduction disorder of the heart.

concepts.preferred_label: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction
concepts.why: The patient has left atrial enlargement and normal left ventricular ejection fraction, which are indicative of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
The patient has dyspnea on exertion and exercise intolerance, which are symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
The patient has dyspnea on exertion, which is a symptom of asthma.
The patient has a medical history of Parkinson disease.
The patient has syncope and difficulty walking, which are symptoms of orthostatic hypotension.

rationales.F05: Elevated blood pressure is a strong indicator for Hypertensive Heart Disease.

rationales.F12: Third-degree AV block is a strong indicator for Atrioventricular Block.
